data.long_meaning: Blanche is a French name that comes from the word blanc, meaning white. In Christian tradition, Blanche is a name that evokes images of the pure and immaculate Virgin Mary, who embodies the perfection and holiness of God.

The name continued to be popular into the modern era, and is still used in France and other French-speaking countries today.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Blanche is a name that evokes the purity and holiness of the Virgin Mary. It is a name that reminds us of the perfection and beauty of God, and the importance of living a pure and virtuous life. It is also a name that connects us to the rich cultural and spiritual heritage of the Catholic Church, which has long held Mary as a model of faith and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Blanche, meaning "the white one," symbolizes purity and innocence in Christian tradition. It evokes images of radiant, spotless souls, shining with the divine light of God. Her name serves as a reminder of the transformative power of faith, as we all strive to become more like the spotless Lamb of God.

historical_references.reference: Blanche of Castile, daughter of Alfonso VIII of León and Castile, became queen of France upon her marriage to Louis VIII in 1223. She is remembered for her strong and capable rule during the Albigensian Crusade.

Blanche of Navarre, a daughter of Sancho the Wise, King of Navarre, and Sancha of Castile, was a queen consort of France from 1328 to 1348 during the reigns of Louis X and Jean II. She played a significant role in the Hundred Years' War between France and England, particularly through her alliance with Edward III of England.
